title: Physiognomy Revisited: How Vision-Language Models Encode Sensitive Attributes Through Image Transformation
abstract: arXiv:2610.35910v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Emergent generative AI technologies, while remarkably beneficial across several tasks and domains, can suffer from unforeseen vulnerabilities and difficult-to-anticipate failure modes. Such failure modes can disparately affect vulnerable communities. This paper investigates two well-known vision language models (VLMs) and inspects how these models encode protected identities while generating images. We show that when VLMs are requested to transform human face images to reflect race identities (e.g., Hispanic, Black, White, or Asian) and sexual orientation (e.g., gay or straight), VLMs often comply with such requests. We demonstrate that compliance (and refusal) is non-deterministic, group-sensitive, and generated images are statistically distinguishable, often accentuating deep-seated stereotypes. We further show that representation biases introduced during image generation can re-emerge in textual reasoning and characterization tasks.

translated_title: 面相学的重现：视觉语言模型如何通过图像变换编码敏感属性
translated_abstract: 新兴的生成式人工智能技术虽然在众多任务和领域中具有显著益处，但也可能存在无法预见的漏洞和难以预测的失败模式。这些失败模式可能对弱势群体造成不成比例的影响。本文研究了两个知名的视觉语言模型（VLM），考察这些模型在生成图像时如何编码受保护的身份特征。我们表明，当要求VLM将人脸图像转换为反映种族身份（如西班牙裔、黑人、白人或亚裔）和性取向（如同性恋或异性恋）时，VLM往往会遵从此类请求。我们证明，这种遵从（和拒绝）是非确定性的、对群体敏感的，且生成的图像在统计上是可区分的，往往会强化根深蒂固的刻板印象。我们进一步表明，图像生成过程中引入的表征偏差可能会在文本推理和人物刻画任务中再次出现。
tldr: 本文揭示了视觉语言模型在图像变换任务中会遵从按种族和性取向改变人脸的请求，生成统计上可区分且强化刻板印象的图像，并且这些表征偏差还会在下游文本推理任务中重现。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that vision-language models often comply with requests to transform face images by race and sexual orientation, producing statistically distinguishable images that reinforce stereotypes, and these representation biases re-emerge in downstream textual reasoning tasks.
